title: Steering the Language Axis: From Linear Decodability to Causal Control
abstract: arXiv:2608.12334v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Despite the impressive multilingual capabilities of Large Language Models, the latent dynamics dictating language selection remain poorly understood. In this work, we ask whether language identity is merely linearly decodable from hidden states, or if it can be causally controlled by a compact activation direction. We conduct an exhaustive causal intervention analysis across multiple model families, including Qwen 3.5-2B and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, isolating PCA-derived "language axes" to perform steering and ablation experiments across 1.26 million generations on the FLORES-200 dataset.   Steering along these geometric directions reliably forces language switching in both cross-script (English to Chinese) and same-script (English to Spanish) settings, whereas equal-magnitude random perturbations yield virtually no effect. Our layerwise analysis reveals that language commitment is highly localized and explicitly language-pair-dependent.

translated_title: 驾驭语言轴：从线性可解码性到因果控制
translated_abstract: 尽管大型语言模型具有令人印象深刻的多语言能力，但决定语言选择的潜在动态仍鲜为人知。在这项工作中，我们探讨了语言身份是否仅能从隐藏状态中线性解码，或者能否通过一个紧凑的激活方向进行因果控制。我们对多个模型家族（包括Qwen 3.5-2B和Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct）进行了详尽的因果干预分析，分离出基于PCA的“语言轴”，并在FLORES-200数据集上进行了超过126万次生成的引导和消融实验。沿这些几何方向的引导能可靠地强制语言切换，无论是在跨文字（英语到中文）还是同文字（英语到西班牙语）场景中，而等幅随机扰动几乎无效。我们的逐层分析揭示，语言承诺具有高度局部性，并明确依赖于语言对。
tldr: 本研究通过因果干预实验证明，大型语言模型中的语言选择可由隐藏状态中的紧凑激活方向（语言轴）因果控制，且该控制具有局部性和语言对依赖性。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates through causal intervention experiments that language selection in large language models can be causally controlled by a compact activation direction (language axis), with the control being highly localized and language-pair-dependent.
